title: Show the smallest Neumann coefficient is 9 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

For every integer `p ≥ 2`, the within-cell Neumann ceiling

```text
U = 8 p^2 (D - 4) / (D - 32 p^2),    D = 2^{32760 p},
```

satisfies `8 p^2 < U < 9 p^2`. The smallest integer `c` with `U < c p^2` for every such `p` is therefore `9`. Every integer `c ≤ 8` fails because `U > 8 p^2`. The same `9 p^2` is strictly sharper than `16 p^2 - 1` and `p^6`.

This is a property of the formula. It is an inverse bound only when the #4452 gauge holds. The ideal gaps stay hypotheses. No new κ. The selected record remains `23/10000`.

This answers the open question of #4492. It does not replay #4452 or #4492. The tensor absorption and the Schur margin still use `10`.

## Comparison

With a positive denominator, `U < 9 p^2` is equivalent to `8(D - 4) < 9(D - 32 p^2)`. The difference is

```text
9(D - 32 p^2) - 8(D - 4) = D - 288 p^2 + 32.
```

So it is enough that `D > 288 p^2 - 32`. For `p ≥ 2`, `2^{2p} ≥ p^2 + 1`, hence `288 p^2 < 2^{2p+9}`. The exponent gap `32760 p - (2p + 9) = 32758 p - 9` is 65507 at `p = 2` and increases, so `2^{2p+9} < D`. The same estimate gives `D > 32 p^2`.
